infrastructure: Montenegro has good urban internet connectivity, particularly in coastal tourism areas.
The country is investing in digital infrastructure as part of EU accession preparations.
Data centre capacity is minimal; the country relies on connectivity to regional hubs.
talent: University of Montenegro has limited AI research capacity.
Small population (620,000) fundamentally constrains the absolute talent pool.
Some Montenegrin IT professionals work remotely for international companies.
governance: Montenegro is the most advanced Western Balkans country in EU accession negotiations.
GDPR-aligned data protection; the Agency for Personal Data Protection is the regulator.
Anti-corruption reforms are progressing as part of EU Chapter 23/24 requirements.
investment: Tourism-driven FDI dominates, with very limited AI-specific investment.
EU pre-accession IPA funds support digital transformation.
Small domestic market limits investment scale.
economic_readiness: A small, tourism-dependent economy with limited industrial AI demand.
Growing digital services sector targeting EU markets.
Low GDP per capita constrains domestic AI adoption.
